text: The account holder, Junaid Akhtar, a salaried textile engineer, has a declared monthly income of PKR 180,000. In the 30‑day period ending 25 May 2026, the account received five inbound IBFT transfers totaling PKR 319,000 from various family members (Bilal Butt, Saad Farooq, Usman Rehman, Tariq Rehman, and an unnamed family member). These amounts far exceed the expected salary inflow and are not matched by any corresponding salary payment from his employer, Shan Textile Mills, which only deposited PKR 180,000 on 3 May. The inbound transfers are clustered in a short time frame (5‑25 May) and originate from accounts that are not linked to the customer’s declared employment or known business activities. Concurrently, the account made several outbound bill payments (PKR 59,000 to Imtiaz Supermarket, PKR 39,000 to PTCL, PKR 30,000 to K‑Electric, PKR 61,000 to Imtiaz Supermarket, PKR 39,000 to K‑Electric) that do not align with the customer’s declared monthly expenses. The velocity of inbound transfers (PKR 319,000 in 23 days) exceeds the 90‑day baseline threshold set by the system (alert threshold 300). This pattern suggests potential layering or structuring to conceal the source of funds, raising suspicion of money‑laundering activity. Therefore, the transaction warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR).
